newsitem.title: USA: Kodak consolidating media buying outfit.
newsitem.headline: Kodak consolidating media buying outfit.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co said Friday that its two worldwide consumer advertising agencies will be pooling their resources when it comes to buying advertising for the company.
J. Walter Thompson and Oglivy & Mather, both members of WPP Group Plc, will continue to develop the advertising campaigns for separate products.
Thompson handles Kodak's consumer film products, while Oglivy concentrates on digital products and corporate advertising.
"They will definitely still manage their own separate assignments and create their own ad campaigns," Kodak spokesman Charles Smith said.

But when it comes time to actually buy advertising, the two companies will go through a separate entity that is to be formed. Kodak said it hopes this new strategy will cut costs and make advertising more efficient by eliminating any overlap, Smith said.
"This is a natural extension of our earlier announced global brand advertising consolidation behind WPP," Eastman Kodak Chief Marketing Officer Carl Gustin said in a statement.

"Together, these agencies represent the largest buyers of media in the world. By joining forces in this way, it allows Kodak to continue to compete effectively for the best possible media placements on a global basis."
The total amount of ad billings to be handled by the group was not available, but Kodak places $250 million worth in the United States alone, according to Advertising Age.

Under the consolidation, Young & Rubicam and a number of local agencies will lose billings to Thompson and Ogilvy, both of which handled some Kodak media in the past. The WPP agencies already handle all of the creative aspects of Kodak's consumer advertising.
